transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled
pros to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, DC, I'm Dale Willman. President Trump was in Georgia today
campaigning for Republicans with just 10 days left before the midterm elections. He defended
his own performance this term, including gas prices that rose dramatically after he attacked Iran.
He also urged Republicans to get out the vote. Former President Barack Obama, meanwhile,
was campaigning in the Midwest Saturday. Speaking in Ohio, he criticized Republican
gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. His campaign has featured an ad that features the
estranged mother of his opponent, Democratic candidate Amy Acton. Obama said there's no line
Ramaswamy will not cross and no low he will not sink to. And in Michigan, he condemned critics
of Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed suggesting they are using his faith to tear him down.
The U.S. Postal Service says it's taking extra steps starting today to make sure mail-in ballots
for the midterm elections are delivered on time. NPR's Hansi Lo Wang has our reports.
The U.S. Postal Service is directing its letter carriers and mail processing plants to pay extra
close attention to mail-in ballots starting today. It's part of what USPS calls its extraordinary
measures for speeding up deliveries for every federal general election. NPR asked if any post
offices are choosing to take any optional measures, like extending opening and closing times, but USPS
did not directly respond. Its required directives are starting more than a month after the Supreme
Court blocked the Trump administration from using USPS to carry out mail-in voting restrictions
for the midterms. Many voting advocates are still concerned about last-minute voters getting their
ballots rejected. If your ballot must be received by your local election office by election day,
USPS recommends mailing it back by this Tuesday, October 27th. Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
An $800 million agreement has been reached with the archdiocese of New York involving
child sex abuse, and Pierre's Chantalice Duster has her story. The archdiocese of New York says
it has agreed to settle sexual abuse claims brought against the church. Archbishop Ronald
Hicks said in an email to archdiocese pre-Saturday afternoon that they are on the verge of being able
to "bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim survivors." Jeff Anderson, an
attorney for some of the plaintiffs, told NPR 1,300 people accepted the $800 million agreement.
It really is a testament to the courage and the persistence of the survivors who stood up, who
spoke up, and who caused the archdiocese of New York to finally reckon to each of them, which is
long past due. Anderson also says survivors feel relief about the settlement and sorrow about the
abuse they faced. Chantalice Duster, NPR News. Clashes erupted in Paris as a mass march drew to
a close Saturday. More than 400,000 people rallied across France over school funding and soaring
living costs. Challenging President Emmanuel Macron, police say that they made nearly 1,000 arrests.
You're listening to NPR News. Ukraine's president says the country's access to Starlink has been
fully restored as of Friday night. Ukraine uses the access for targeting as well as its defense
against drone launches from Russia. President Vladimir Zelensky had said previously the Elon
Musk-owned Starlink had shut off its access. As the cost of living rises, Americans are spending
more on lottery tickets. As NPR's John Stoleness reports, the hope of huge payouts are at the heart
of it. Americans spent an average of $323 on lottery tickets, according to census data from
2024, the most recent year in which figures are available. That was up 4.5% from two years prior.
An analysis from Lending Tree found more than $110 billion was spent on lottery tickets overall,
thanks in large part to more huge payouts. 15 jackpots have surpassed a billion dollars
since the first in January of 2016, but 13 of those have happened in the last five years.
However, lottery spending fell in 28 states, with the largest decreases in Wyoming and Oklahoma.
But larger increases in fewer states led by North Carolina and Virginia pushed up national spending
overall. John Stoleness, NPR News. There were more upsets today in college football's top 10,
as unranked UCF beat BYU 39-31. Kayon Jenkins threw a two-yard touchdown pass for the win in
the second overtime. Unranked Cincinnati also beat No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24. No. 1 Miami easily
handled Pittsburgh 52-23, and No. 6 Indiana slipped past Michigan. And Albany beat Rhode Island 38-21.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from Rosetta Stone,
offering an alternative approach to language learning. Without relying on traditional
memorization, the platform guides users to intuitively think in a second language.
More information at RosettaStone.com.

USPS directs carriers to prioritize mail-in ballots for midterms, recommends mailing back by October 27
New York archdiocese agrees to $800 million settlement over child sex abuse claims
Clashes erupt in Paris as 400,000 rally across France over school funding and living costs
